blocks.text: GLOSSARY
This glossary of annelid terminology is an edited and shortened version of that written by Glasby et al. (2000) and Rouse and Pleije}

abdomen: body region posterior to the thorax. Varies among
annelid groups and should not be generally regarded as indi-
cating homologous regions.

abranchial: without branchiae.
abyssal: oceanic waters between depths of 4000 m and 6000 m.
achaetous: without chaetac.

acicula, aciculae: stout supportive chaeta found internally in
projecting parapodial rami.

acicular chaeta: stout, projecting chaeta.
acrosome: membrane limited organelle at apex of sperma-
tozoon head, covering the anterior surface of the nucleus;
secretes enzymes thought to facilitate sperm entry.
adelphophagy: consumption by a developing larva of nurse
eggs present in the same egg capsule.
aileron: accessory jaw plate in Glyceridae.
aliform: elongate narrow lobe, used to refer to a pair of notopo-
dia of some Chaetopteridae.
anal plaque: depressed (or sunken) plate-like pygidium of some
Maldanidae and other annelids.
anal sacs: paired posterior evaginations from the hindgut in
Thalassematidae, possibly homologous with metanephridia.
androecium: small cavity within the metanephridial sac of
Bonelliinae, where the dwarf males are often found,

annulated: ringed or marked with grooves delineating seg-
ments.
antenna, antennae: sensory projection arising from the dorsal,
lateral, or frontal surface of the prostomium.
antennular auricle: see auricule.
anterior cirri: dorsal and/or ventral cirti of parapodia of
cephalized segments; often more elongate than those of more
posterior parapodia; confused in the literature with peristomi-
al cirri, (See tentacular cirri).
anterior cirri formula: notation indicating the arrangement of
the anterior cirri and chaetae; originally used for Phyllodocidae,
now also extended to other Phyllodocida.
apical tooth: see primary tooth.
apodous: segments without parapodia.
apomorphy: a derived, or less general state; see synapomorphy
and compare with plesiomorphy.
arborescent: branching like a tree.
architomy: form of schizotomy involving fragmentation of the

body, without any prior cephalization of the various frag-
ments; compare with paratomy.

aristate chaeta: simple chaeta with smooth shaft and a tuft of
hairs or a single spine.

article: demarcated sections of chaetae or cirri separated by
joints.

articulate: jointed, as in antennae, tentacular cirri, palps, and
dorsal cirri.
achaetigerous: see achaetous.

atoke: non-sexual, unmodified state of an individual; pertaining
to taxa that undergo epitoky.

auricule: paired ear-shaped processes at the base of an antenna
(ceratophore) characteristic of some Sigalionidae.

avicular: beaked; shaped like a bird’s head; used to describe
hooked chaetae, uncini.

B
basal lappet: see auricule.
benthic: pertaining to the sea floor.

biarticulate: with two joints; pertaining to antennae, tentacular
cirri, palps, and dorsal cirri.
bidentate chaeta: chacta with two teeth distally.
bifid: distally split in two.
bifurcate chaeta: simple chaeta with two prongs.
bilimbate chaeta: simple chaeta with two wings; see limbate.

biramous parapodium: parapodium with two branches, a
notopodium and a neuropodium.

blade: distal, flattened portion of a compound or simple
chaeta.

boss: small projection or knob-like process in compound and
simple chaetae.

brain: ganglionic mass situated at least in part in the prostomi-
um.

branchia, branchiae: extension of the body wall with a loop
of the vascular system; usually well equipped with capillary
blood-vessels.

branchial crown: see radiolar crown.
branchiferous: term referring to segments bearing branchiae.
brush-tipped chaeta: simple chacta with a brush-like tip (also
known as penicillate chaeta).
buccal cavity: mouth cavity.
buccal organ: anterior part of alimentary canal derived from
the larval stomodeum, comprising a complex set of folds,
musculature, and glands; see pharynx.
